title: Aaron Dessner Talks Longevity in the Music Industry — and His New Label With Interscope
summary: In the latest episode of Billboard On the Record, Aaron Dessner talks about the art of collaboration, his journey in the music business and his new label, Long Pond Music.
body: Aaron Dessner has been in the music industry for about 25 years as part of the acclaimed independent rock band The National , but the last few years have been his most ambitious yet. He’s still part of the band, but he’s also become the go-to collaborator for some of the biggest acts in the world, from Taylor Swift to Noah Kahan , Gracie Abrams , Mumford & Sons and Ed Sheeran — shaping the sound of modern pop in the process. Collaborators of Dessner often come to him and work from his studio and home, Long Pond, in the Hudson Valley of upstate New York. “Long Pond feels like an instrument in itself, where there’s a lot of inherent magic there,” Dessner tells Billboard . It’s become an almost mythological place in popular culture, thanks to Swift’s long pond studio sessions for her album Folklore, which was created with Dessner during the COVID-19 lockdown. To build on the lore of the studio, Dessner is now launching a new record label, Long Pond Music, with Interscope Records, hoping to bring that same magic to more artists in need of a place for development. title: Gmail is turning its stars and importance markers blue, and users aren’t happy
summary: Google says the change helps with accessibility, but users complain it flattens hierarchy and clutters the inbox.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google replaced Gmail’s default yellow stars and yellow importance chevrons with high-contrast, saturated blue markers to improve accessibility. However, users complain that the identical blue tones flatten the visual hierarchy, make email scanning harder, and add visual clutter. While there’s no way to revert the changes, you can manually select a yellow star preset (and re-star items) or hide importance chevrons entirely in Settings. Google is rolling out a visual overhaul to Gmail on the web, replacing its longstanding yellow stars and importance markers with a bright, high-contrast blue. While Gmail has gained plenty of genuinely practical upgrades recently, such as letting you copy 2FA codes directly without opening emails or leveraging AI overview search capabilities , this particular color switch has annoyed desktop users who rely on quick visual cues to scan their messages. In a post on X , the official Gmail team confirmed the change, explaining that it updated the default star and “Important” label colors from yellow to blue to meet modern accessibility standards and ensure inboxes are easier to read and more inclusive.
